Definition: a multitude; also offspring; specifically interest (on capital)
BiblicalUsage: marbîyth is a multitude, an increase, and sometimes interest on capital. In 2 Chronicles 30:18 a multitude of the people eat the passover though they have not cleansed themselves, and Hezekiah prays for them. In 1 Samuel 2:33 the increase of Eli's house shall die in the flower of their age, and in 2 Chronicles 9:6 the queen of Sheba says the one half of the greatness of Solomon's wisdom was not told her. The word is more than expected, for good or for ill.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe marbîyth shows me that God measures increase exactly. I hold that the greatness of His wisdom is always more than I was told.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
